about.title: San Juan Bautista Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Juan Bautista sees a modest but real share of injury collisions each year, with public records showing crashes clustering on SR-156, SR-156 Westbound, Rt 156, and The Alameda Road, often on Sunday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. when travelers pass through this small San Benito County community. Even a low-speed impact on these corridors can leave someone with lasting pain, medical bills, and missed work. We handle personal injury claims for people hurt in San Juan Bautista crashes. Our team can evaluate the details of what happened, deal with insurance adjusters, and help protect your claim from early mistakes. Because California courts apply pure comparative fault, how a claim is documented and communicated matters from the very first phone call. Our service is free to use, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why San Juan Bautista Residents Choose Us

items.title: California's Fault Rules Are Complicated
items.desc: Because California follows pure comparative fault, an insurer may try to shift blame onto you to reduce what they pay. We can push back on unfair fault assessments from the start.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but claims involving a government road or agency can require notice in as little as six months. Getting guidance early helps avoid missing a critical deadline.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Hurt Your Claim
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash, hoping to lock in details before you know the full extent of your injuries. We can handle that communication so nothing you say is used against you later.

items.question: Do I need to talk to the other driver's insurance company right away?
items.answer: No, you're not required to give the other insurer a recorded statement, and doing so early can work against you before you understand your injuries fully. It's generally safer to let us handle those conversations. This is one of the most common early mistakes people make after a crash.

items.question: Sunday evenings seem to have more crashes near San Juan Bautista. Does that affect my claim?
items.answer: Public crash records show reported collisions in the area tend to cluster on Sunday evenings, but the time of day alone doesn't determine fault or the value of a claim. What matters most is the evidence gathered, like witness accounts, photos, and official reports. We can help make sure that evidence is preserved regardless of when the crash happened.

items.question: How much does it cost to use your service?
items.answer: Nothing. Our consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
